paragraphs.title: The Law of Cleansing the Leper

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses at the beginning of the passage?
answers: The Lord
The priest
The leper
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “The Lord spoke to Moses.”

easy.question: To whom is the leper brought on the day of his cleansing?
answers: The camp
The priest
Moses
easy.explanation: The passage says, “He shall be brought unto the priest.”

easy.question: Where does the priest go?
answers: To the leper’s house
To Jerusalem
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: The priest goes “out of the camp.”

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: The leper is brought to the priest, and the priest goes outside the camp to examine him
The priest enters the camp, and then the leper leaves
Moses examines the plague, and then the priest speaks
medium.explanation: First the leper is brought to the priest; then the priest goes outside the camp to examine him.

medium.question: What does “out of the camp” mean?
answers: Inside the camp
Beyond the camp
Above the camp
medium.explanation: It means outside or beyond the camp’s boundaries.

medium.question: Why does the priest go outside the camp?
answers: To speak with Moses
To bring the leper into the camp
To see whether the leprosy has been healed
medium.explanation: The priest examines whether the leprosy has been healed.

challenge.question: What condition does the priest check before the cleansing continues?
answers: That the leprosy has been healed
That the leper has entered the camp
That the leper spoke with Moses
challenge.explanation: The priest checks whether the leprosy has been healed in the leper.

challenge.question: What important fact follows from the priest going outside the camp?
answers: The priest does not need to see the leper
The leper is still outside the camp during the examination
The leper is already completely clean
challenge.explanation: The priest goes outside to examine the leper there, before the leper returns to the camp.

challenge.question: What does the priest see when the passage says the plague is healed in the leper?
answers: That the leper found a new home
That the leper brought an offering
That the leprosy has been healed from the leper’s body
challenge.explanation: The plague has been healed from the person who had it.

questions.question: What condition does the priest check before the cleansing continues?
answers: That the leprosy has been healed
That the leper has entered the camp
That the leper spoke with Moses
questions.explanation: The priest checks whether the leprosy has been healed in the leper.

questions.question: What important fact follows from the priest going outside the camp?
answers: The priest does not need to see the leper
The leper is still outside the camp during the examination
The leper is already completely clean
questions.explanation: The priest goes outside to examine the leper there, before the leper returns to the camp.

questions.question: What does the priest see when the passage says the plague is healed in the leper?
answers: That the leper found a new home
That the leper brought an offering
That the leprosy has been healed from the leper’s body
questions.explanation: The plague has been healed from the person who had it.

paragraphs.title: The Ceremony of the Two Birds

easy.question: Who commands the cleansing ceremony?
answers: The priest
The leper
The head of the family
easy.explanation: The priest commands the ceremony.

easy.question: How many birds are required?
answers: One bird
Two birds
Three birds
easy.explanation: The priest takes two living, clean birds.

easy.question: What happens to the living bird at the end?
answers: It is killed
It is returned to a cage
It is released into the open field
easy.explanation: The living bird is released into the open field.

medium.question: What is the first step in the ceremony?
answers: One bird is killed
The living bird is released
The person is sprinkled seven times
medium.explanation: First, one bird is killed in an earthen vessel over running water.

medium.question: What does “running water” mean here?
answers: Water colored with blood
Flowing or fresh water
Water in a sealed container
medium.explanation: “Running water” means natural, flowing, or fresh water.

medium.question: What is dipped with the living bird into the blood?
answers: Gold, silver, and oil
Bread, wine, and salt
Cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop
medium.explanation: The cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop are dipped with the living bird.

challenge.question: What distinguishes the two birds?
answers: One is killed and the other remains alive
One is clean and the other unclean
One is large and the other small
challenge.explanation: One bird is killed, while the other is specifically called the living bird.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes the blood, water, and living bird?
answers: The living bird drinks the water before the other bird is killed
The living bird and the materials are dipped in the slain bird’s blood over running water
The blood is poured on the living bird after it is released
challenge.explanation: The living bird and the materials are dipped in the slain bird’s blood over running water.

challenge.question: What happens after the priest sprinkles the person seven times?
answers: He kills both birds
He puts the living bird back in the vessel
He declares the person clean and releases the living bird
challenge.explanation: The person is pronounced clean, and the living bird is released.

questions.question: What distinguishes the two birds?
answers: One is killed and the other remains alive
One is clean and the other unclean
One is large and the other small
questions.explanation: One bird is killed, while the other is specifically called the living bird.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the blood, water, and living bird?
answers: The living bird drinks the water before the other bird is killed
The living bird and the materials are dipped in the slain bird’s blood over running water
The blood is poured on the living bird after it is released
questions.explanation: The living bird and the materials are dipped in the slain bird’s blood over running water.

questions.question: What happens after the priest sprinkles the person seven times?
answers: He kills both birds
He puts the living bird back in the vessel
He declares the person clean and releases the living bird
questions.explanation: The person is pronounced clean, and the living bird is released.

easy.question: What does the person do before entering the camp?
answers: He washes his clothes, shaves his hair, and washes in water
He offers a sacrifice and immediately enters his tent
He remains outside the camp forever
easy.explanation: He washes his clothes, shaves his hair, and washes in water.

easy.question: How long does he remain outside his tent?
answers: Three days
Seven days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: He remains outside his tent for seven days.

easy.question: What does he do on the seventh day?
answers: He enters his tent without washing
He stops the cleansing process
He shaves all his hair, washes his clothes, and washes his flesh
easy.explanation: On the seventh day he shaves, washes his clothes, and washes his flesh.

medium.question: What is the order of events in verse 8?
answers: Washing and shaving, bathing, entering the camp, and staying outside the tent
Entering the tent, shaving, and then leaving the camp
Staying outside the tent, entering the camp, and then washing
medium.explanation: He first washes, shaves, and bathes; then he enters the camp but remains outside his tent.

medium.question: What does “the one to be cleansed” mean in this passage?
answers: Someone who teaches others to be clean
Someone undergoing the cleansing process
Someone who has left the camp
medium.explanation: It refers to a person who is in the process of being cleansed.

medium.question: What can we understand from his entering the camp but staying outside his tent?
answers: He may not enter anywhere
He is immediately fully cleansed
He may be in the camp but has not fully returned to normal life
medium.explanation: His return takes place gradually: he enters the camp but remains outside his tent.

challenge.question: Which specific hair is mentioned among the hair shaved on the seventh day?
answers: His eyebrows
The hair on his arms
The hair on his legs
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically mentions the hair of his head, beard, and eyebrows.

challenge.question: What does the repeated shaving on the seventh day show?
answers: The first shaving was forbidden
Cleansing takes several stages and is not immediate
He must regrow his hair before bathing
challenge.explanation: The repeated actions show that the cleansing process continues in stages.

challenge.question: What change in status occurs during the process?
answers: He moves immediately from outside the camp into his tent
He goes from being unable to bathe to being forbidden to enter the camp
He moves from initial washing and shaving to completing the cleansing on the seventh day
challenge.explanation: The seventh day completes the cleansing process with further washing and shaving.

questions.question: Which specific hair is mentioned among the hair shaved on the seventh day?
answers: His eyebrows
The hair on his arms
The hair on his legs
questions.explanation: The passage specifically mentions the hair of his head, beard, and eyebrows.

questions.question: What does the repeated shaving on the seventh day show?
answers: The first shaving was forbidden
Cleansing takes several stages and is not immediate
He must regrow his hair before bathing
questions.explanation: The repeated actions show that the cleansing process continues in stages.

questions.question: What change in status occurs during the process?
answers: He moves immediately from outside the camp into his tent
He goes from being unable to bathe to being forbidden to enter the camp
He moves from initial washing and shaving to completing the cleansing on the seventh day
questions.explanation: The seventh day completes the cleansing process with further washing and shaving.

paragraphs.title: The Offerings on the Eighth Day

easy.question: What does the cleansed person bring on the eighth day?
answers: Two male lambs, one ewe lamb, fine flour, and oil
One bull and two doves
Only one lamb
easy.explanation: He brings two male lambs, one ewe lamb, fine flour mixed with oil, and a log of oil.

easy.question: Where does the priest present the person?
answers: Inside the house
At the door of the tabernacle
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: The priest presents him before the Lord at the tabernacle entrance.

easy.question: How much oil is required?
answers: Three-tenths of an ephah
Two measures
One log
easy.explanation: The offering includes one log of oil.

medium.question: What does the priest do after presenting the man before the Lord?
answers: He takes one male lamb and the log of oil, offers and waves them
He sends the man home
He immediately kills all the lambs
medium.explanation: The priest offers one lamb as a trespass offering and waves it with the oil.

medium.question: What does “without blemish” mean?
answers: Very young
Without defect
Owned by the priest
medium.explanation: It means whole and free from defect, as required for a sacrifice.

medium.question: Where is the trespass offering killed, and what does this show?
answers: At the house, so it is only a private offering
Outside the camp, so it is not holy
Where the sin and burnt offerings are killed, because it is most holy
medium.explanation: It is killed in the holy place where the other offerings are killed and is called most holy.

challenge.question: Why is the trespass offering killed where the sin and burnt offerings are killed?
answers: The law compares the trespass offering to the sin offering
There was no other place in the sanctuary
The lamb could not be killed elsewhere
challenge.explanation: The passage says the trespass offering is treated like the sin offering in this matter.

challenge.question: Which animal is used for the trespass offering?
answers: The year-old ewe lamb
One of the two male lambs
All three animals together
challenge.explanation: The priest takes one of the two male lambs for the trespass offering.

challenge.question: How is the trespass offering described at the end of the passage?
answers: It is eaten outside the camp
It belongs to the cleansed man
It is like the sin offering, belongs to the priest, and is most holy
challenge.explanation: The passage says it is like the sin offering, belongs to the priest, and is most holy.

questions.question: Why is the trespass offering killed where the sin and burnt offerings are killed?
answers: The law compares the trespass offering to the sin offering
There was no other place in the sanctuary
The lamb could not be killed elsewhere
questions.explanation: The passage says the trespass offering is treated like the sin offering in this matter.

questions.question: Which animal is used for the trespass offering?
answers: The year-old ewe lamb
One of the two male lambs
All three animals together
questions.explanation: The priest takes one of the two male lambs for the trespass offering.

questions.question: How is the trespass offering described at the end of the passage?
answers: It is eaten outside the camp
It belongs to the cleansed man
It is like the sin offering, belongs to the priest, and is most holy
questions.explanation: The passage says it is like the sin offering, belongs to the priest, and is most holy.

paragraphs.title: Blood and Oil Applied to the Cleansed Person

easy.question: Who takes the blood of the trespass offering and applies it to the person?
answers: The priest
The cleansed person
The Levite
easy.explanation: The passage says, “The priest shall take some of the blood.”

easy.question: How many times does the priest sprinkle the oil before the Lord?
answers: Three times
Seven times
Once
easy.explanation: He sprinkles the oil seven times.

easy.question: Where does the priest put the remaining oil?
answers: On the person’s hand
On his foot
On his head
easy.explanation: The remaining oil is poured on the head of the person being cleansed.

medium.question: What does the priest do after pouring oil into his left palm?
answers: He dips his right finger in it and sprinkles it seven times
He immediately offers the burnt offering
He puts all the oil on the man’s head
medium.explanation: He dips his right finger into the oil and sprinkles it seven times before the Lord.

medium.question: What does “the rest of the oil” mean?
answers: The first oil used
The oil that remains
New oil
medium.explanation: It means the oil left in the priest’s hand after the sprinkling.

medium.question: What is the order of the offerings?
answers: Burnt offering, sin offering, grain offering
Grain offering, burnt offering, sin offering
Sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering
medium.explanation: The priest first offers the sin offering, then the burnt offering, followed by the grain offering.

challenge.question: Where are both the blood and the oil applied?
answers: The right ear, right thumb, and right great toe
The left ear, palm, and forehead
Both ears, both hands, and both feet
challenge.explanation: Both are applied to the right ear, right thumb, and right great toe.

challenge.question: What does the use of oil in several stages show?
answers: All the oil is poured on the altar at once
Some oil is sprinkled, and the rest is applied to the person and his head
The oil is only for lighting a fire
challenge.explanation: Some oil is used for sprinkling, and the remainder is applied to the person and his head.

challenge.question: When is the person declared clean?
answers: Immediately after the blood is put on his ear
After the oil is poured into the priest’s palm
After the burnt and grain offerings are offered and atonement is made
challenge.explanation: After the offerings and atonement, the passage says, “He shall be clean.”

questions.question: Where are both the blood and the oil applied?
answers: The right ear, right thumb, and right great toe
The left ear, palm, and forehead
Both ears, both hands, and both feet
questions.explanation: Both are applied to the right ear, right thumb, and right great toe.

questions.question: What does the use of oil in several stages show?
answers: All the oil is poured on the altar at once
Some oil is sprinkled, and the rest is applied to the person and his head
The oil is only for lighting a fire
questions.explanation: Some oil is used for sprinkling, and the remainder is applied to the person and his head.

questions.question: When is the person declared clean?
answers: Immediately after the blood is put on his ear
After the oil is poured into the priest’s palm
After the burnt and grain offerings are offered and atonement is made
questions.explanation: After the offerings and atonement, the passage says, “He shall be clean.”

paragraphs.title: The Offering for a Poor Person

easy.question: What is the person’s situation at the beginning of verse 21?
answers: He is poor and cannot afford the full offering
He is very sick
He is a priest
easy.explanation: The verse says, “If he be poor, and cannot get so much.”

easy.question: How many lambs must he bring for a trespass offering?
answers: Two lambs
One lamb
Three lambs
easy.explanation: He must bring one lamb for a trespass offering.

easy.question: When does he bring the offerings to the priest?
answers: The first day
The seventh day
The eighth day
easy.explanation: The passage says he brings them on the eighth day.

medium.question: What are the two turtledoves or young pigeons used for?
answers: One for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering
Both for a trespass offering
Both for a grain offering
medium.explanation: One is for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.

medium.question: What does “such as he is able to get” mean?
answers: He must catch them himself
He brings what he can afford or obtain
He must bring them only from Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to what the poor person is able to obtain.

medium.question: To whom and where are the offerings brought?
answers: To the king at the palace
To a Levite outside the camp
To the priest at the tabernacle entrance
medium.explanation: They are brought to the priest at the door of the tabernacle before the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “such as he is able to get” imply about the birds?
answers: He may choose between turtledoves and young pigeons according to his means
He may bring only one bird
He must bring both turtledoves and pigeons
challenge.explanation: The law allows either kind according to what the person can obtain.

challenge.question: What important distinction is made between the two birds?
answers: They serve the same purpose
One is a sin offering and the other a burnt offering
They replace the trespass-offering lamb
challenge.explanation: One bird is designated for each of these two offerings; they do not replace the lamb.

challenge.question: Which offering is still required of the poor person?
answers: Two grain offerings
Two lambs
One lamb for a trespass offering
challenge.explanation: Even the poor person must bring one lamb for a trespass offering.

questions.question: What does “such as he is able to get” imply about the birds?
answers: He may choose between turtledoves and young pigeons according to his means
He may bring only one bird
He must bring both turtledoves and pigeons
questions.explanation: The law allows either kind according to what the person can obtain.

questions.question: What important distinction is made between the two birds?
answers: They serve the same purpose
One is a sin offering and the other a burnt offering
They replace the trespass-offering lamb
questions.explanation: One bird is designated for each of these two offerings; they do not replace the lamb.

questions.question: Which offering is still required of the poor person?
answers: Two grain offerings
Two lambs
One lamb for a trespass offering
questions.explanation: Even the poor person must bring one lamb for a trespass offering.

easy.question: What does the priest take with the trespass-offering lamb?
answers: A log of oil
Two pigeons
A bowl of blood
easy.explanation: The priest takes the lamb and a log of oil.

easy.question: On how many places does the priest apply the blood?
answers: One place
Three places
Seven places
easy.explanation: The blood is put on the ear, thumb, and great toe on the right side.

easy.question: What does the priest do with the oil on his finger?
answers: He pours it on the ground
He rubs it on the lamb
He sprinkles it seven times before the Lord
easy.explanation: He sprinkles the oil seven times before the Lord.

medium.question: Why is the oil put on the same places as the blood?
answers: To add to the cleansing ceremony
To mark the priest
To measure the oil
medium.explanation: The shared locations connect the blood and oil portions of the ceremony.

medium.question: What does “wave offering” mean?
answers: Raising or moving an offering ceremonially before the Lord
Killing the offering quickly
Setting the offering aside
medium.explanation: It refers to ceremonially presenting or lifting the offering before the Lord.

medium.question: What happens to the oil remaining afterward?
answers: It is poured on the altar
It is put on the person’s head
It is put on the priest’s ear
medium.explanation: The remaining oil is put on the head of the person being cleansed.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the ceremony includes a repeated, precise action?
answers: The oil is sprinkled seven times before the Lord
The lamb is taken
The lamb is killed
challenge.explanation: The repeated sprinkling seven times is a precise ritual action.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “according to what he is able to get” imply about the birds?
answers: Everyone must bring both kinds
The offering may be chosen according to the person’s means
Only the priest may choose the birds
challenge.explanation: The offering is adjusted to the person’s ability to obtain it.

challenge.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Oil on the head, then blood, then killing
Killing and applying blood, then sprinkling and applying oil
Applying oil, choosing the lamb, then waving it
challenge.explanation: The lamb is killed and its blood applied first; then the oil is sprinkled and applied.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the ceremony includes a repeated, precise action?
answers: The oil is sprinkled seven times before the Lord
The lamb is taken
The lamb is killed
questions.explanation: The repeated sprinkling seven times is a precise ritual action.

questions.question: What does the phrase “according to what he is able to get” imply about the birds?
answers: Everyone must bring both kinds
The offering may be chosen according to the person’s means
Only the priest may choose the birds
questions.explanation: The offering is adjusted to the person’s ability to obtain it.

questions.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Oil on the head, then blood, then killing
Killing and applying blood, then sprinkling and applying oil
Applying oil, choosing the lamb, then waving it
questions.explanation: The lamb is killed and its blood applied first; then the oil is sprinkled and applied.

paragraphs.title: The Poor Person’s Offering and Cleansing

easy.question: What does the person offer according to his means?
answers: A sin offering and a burnt offering
Only a grain offering
Only a sin offering
easy.explanation: He brings a sin offering and a burnt offering according to what he can afford.

easy.question: Who makes atonement for the person being cleansed?
answers: The person himself
The priest
The people
easy.explanation: The verse says that the priest makes atonement for him.

easy.question: Who is described in verse 32?
answers: The priest
A wealthy person
Someone with leprosy who cannot afford the regular offering
easy.explanation: The verse concerns a person with leprosy who cannot afford the regular offering.

medium.question: Why is the person’s financial ability mentioned?
answers: To excuse him from every offering
To match the offering to what he can obtain
To require a more expensive offering
medium.explanation: The offering is adjusted to what the person can afford.

medium.question: What happens after the offerings are brought?
answers: He goes home without further action
He develops a new plague
The priest makes atonement for him before the Lord
medium.explanation: The priest makes atonement for the cleansed person.

medium.question: What does “according to what he can afford” mean here?
answers: What he can obtain or pay for
What he can see from far away
What he must hold in his hand
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the person’s financial ability.

challenge.question: What is the connection between verses 31 and 32?
answers: Verse 32 cancels the offerings in verse 31
Verse 32 discusses the priest instead of the cleansed person
Verse 32 explains what happens when a person cannot afford the regular offering
challenge.explanation: Verse 32 addresses the case of someone unable to afford the regular offering.

challenge.question: What follows from the poor person still being required to be cleansed?
answers: His financial situation changes the offering but does not cancel cleansing
Only wealthy people must be cleansed
The poor person needs no atonement
challenge.explanation: The offering is adjusted, but the cleansing and atonement remain required.

challenge.question: What does the order of the offerings followed by atonement show?
answers: Atonement happens before the offerings
The offerings come before the priest’s act of atonement
The grain offering replaces the other offerings
challenge.explanation: The offerings are mentioned first, and then the priest makes atonement.

questions.question: What is the connection between verses 31 and 32?
answers: Verse 32 cancels the offerings in verse 31
Verse 32 discusses the priest instead of the cleansed person
Verse 32 explains what happens when a person cannot afford the regular offering
questions.explanation: Verse 32 addresses the case of someone unable to afford the regular offering.

questions.question: What follows from the poor person still being required to be cleansed?
answers: His financial situation changes the offering but does not cancel cleansing
Only wealthy people must be cleansed
The poor person needs no atonement
questions.explanation: The offering is adjusted, but the cleansing and atonement remain required.

questions.question: What does the order of the offerings followed by atonement show?
answers: Atonement happens before the offerings
The offerings come before the priest’s act of atonement
The grain offering replaces the other offerings
questions.explanation: The offerings are mentioned first, and then the priest makes atonement.

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Joshua and Caleb
The priests only
easy.explanation: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron.

easy.question: Which land would the Israelites enter?
answers: Egypt
Canaan
Edom
easy.explanation: The passage speaks of entering the land of Canaan.

easy.question: What does the homeowner do when he sees a plague in the house?
answers: He destroys the house immediately
He ignores it
He reports it to the priest
easy.explanation: The homeowner comes and tells the priest.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The priest arrives, then the homeowner sees the plague
The homeowner sees what appears to be a plague and reports it to the priest
Israel leaves the land, and then the priest is sent
medium.explanation: The homeowner first notices the suspected plague and then reports it.

medium.question: What does “the land of your possession” mean?
answers: Land they plan to conquer
Land they are merely visiting
Land given to them as a possession and inheritance
medium.explanation: It refers to the land given to Israel as an inheritance.

medium.question: Why does the homeowner say, “It seems to me there is a plague”?
answers: He reports a suspicion rather than making a final judgment
He has already completed the priest’s examination
He wants the priest to build a new house
medium.explanation: He reports what appears suspicious and leaves the judgment to the priest.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “I put the plague in a house” imply?
answers: Every house in Canaan will be infected
Only priests’ houses can be infected
The plague is presented as something under the Lord’s control
challenge.explanation: The wording presents the plague as something the Lord brings or permits.

challenge.question: What does the Lord’s speaking to both Moses and Aaron suggest?
answers: The matter concerns both leadership and priestly service
Only Moses may examine house plagues
Aaron must leave the priesthood
challenge.explanation: Moses represents leadership and Aaron represents the priesthood.

challenge.question: Which phrase emphasizes that the house is in land given to Israel?
answers: “And he shall tell”
“The land of your possession”
“It seems to me”
challenge.explanation: That phrase identifies the land as Israel’s allotted possession.

questions.question: What does the phrase “I put the plague in a house” imply?
answers: Every house in Canaan will be infected
Only priests’ houses can be infected
The plague is presented as something under the Lord’s control
questions.explanation: The wording presents the plague as something the Lord brings or permits.

questions.question: What does the Lord’s speaking to both Moses and Aaron suggest?
answers: The matter concerns both leadership and priestly service
Only Moses may examine house plagues
Aaron must leave the priesthood
questions.explanation: Moses represents leadership and Aaron represents the priesthood.

questions.question: Which phrase emphasizes that the house is in land given to Israel?
answers: “And he shall tell”
“The land of your possession”
“It seems to me”
questions.explanation: That phrase identifies the land as Israel’s allotted possession.

easy.question: Who commands that the house be emptied?
answers: The priest
The homeowner
The neighbors
easy.explanation: The priest commands them to empty the house.

easy.question: What does the priest examine after the house is emptied?
answers: The household objects
The plague in the walls
The members of the household
easy.explanation: He examines the plague in the walls.

easy.question: How long is the house shut up?
answers: One day
Three days
Seven days
easy.explanation: The house is shut up for seven days.

medium.question: Why is the house emptied before the priest enters?
answers: So the priest can clean it
So that nothing in the house becomes unclean
So the homeowner can move elsewhere
medium.explanation: The house is emptied so that its contents will not become unclean.

medium.question: What is the correct order?
answers: The house is emptied, the priest examines it, and then it is shut up
The house is shut up, emptied, and then examined
The priest examines it, it is emptied, and then shut up
medium.explanation: They empty the house, the priest examines it, and then he shuts it up.

medium.question: What does “hollow streaks” mean in this context?
answers: Bright spots
Long cracks
Sunken or depressed places
medium.explanation: The phrase describes marks that appear lower than the wall.

challenge.question: Which description matches the plague?
answers: Black spots raised above the wall
Greenish or reddish depressions lower than the wall
White, straight cracks
challenge.explanation: The plague appears as greenish or reddish hollow streaks lower than the wall.

challenge.question: What follows from the priest leaving the house and then shutting it up?
answers: The house is examined empty, and entry is restricted afterward
The priest may never enter the house
The house was already clean
